newsitem.title: USA: USDA mulls contract poultry grower regulations.
newsitem.headline: USDA mulls contract poultry grower regulations.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday it was seeking public comment on whether new regulations were needed to address concerns by contract poultry growers about payment and other industry practices.
The move is part of USDA's ongoing effort to tackle concentration in the meat industry.

"The department has heard repeated concerns from poultry growers, who say that they are treated unfairly by the poultry companies with whom they contract," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement.

Specifically, USDA said it is seeking comments on the practice of grower payments tied to the performance of other growers; the accuracy of feed weights, and feed delivery and pickup procedures; and procedures for weighing live birds.
The department published an advance notice of proposed rulemaking in the Federal Register. Comments are due by May 12.

"The comments we receive will enable us to determine whether, and what type, of additional regulatory action may be necessary to protect contract poultry growers in this era of increasing concentration in agriculture," Glickman said.

Currently, contract poultry growers are usually paid under a system that compares a grower's results to that of other growers during a specified time period. Some say comparison of their production costs against production costs of other growers in determining their payment is unfair.
